questions.text: How many moles are present in 8 g of oxygen gas, O₂? [O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of O₂ = 32 g/mol, so amount = 8 ÷ 32 = 0.25 mol.

questions.text: A compound contains 40% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its empirical formula is [C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mole ratios: C = 40/12 = 3.33, H = 6.7/1 = 6.7, O = 53.3/16 = 3.33, giving the simplest ratio 1:2:1, i.e. CH₂O.

questions.text: In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, the mass of water formed from 4 g of hydrogen is [H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: 4 g of H₂ is 2 moles, which forms 2 moles of water: 2 × 18 = 36 g.

questions.text: The volume occupied by 0.5 mole of carbon(IV) oxide at standard temperature and pressure is [molar volume = 22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: Volume = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 dm³ at s.t.p.

questions.text: The vapour density of a gas is 22. Its relative molecular mass is
questions.explanation: Relative molecular mass = 2 × vapour density = 2 × 22 = 44.

questions.text: Using the ideal gas equation PV = nRT, the volume occupied by 1 mole of an ideal gas at 273 K and 1 atm pressure is approximately [R = 0.0821 dm³ atm/mol K]
questions.explanation: V = nRT/P = 1 × 0.0821 × 273 ÷ 1 = 22.4 dm³, the molar volume at s.t.p.

questions.text: The electron configuration of an element with atomic number 17 is
questions.explanation: Chlorine has 17 electrons, arranged 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second and 7 in the third shell.

questions.text: The shape of the ammonia molecule, NH₃, is
questions.explanation: NH₃ has three bonding pairs and one lone pair on nitrogen, giving a pyramidal shape with bond angles of about 107°.

questions.text: Across a period in the periodic table from left to right, the atomic radius generally
questions.explanation: Increasing nuclear charge pulls the same shells closer to the nucleus, so atomic size decreases across a period.

questions.text: Isotopes of the same element differ in their number of
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons (same atomic number) but different numbers of neutrons, hence different mass numbers.

questions.text: The mass of sodium hydroxide [NaOH = 40] in 250 cm³ of a 0.2 mol/dm³ solution is
The ionic equation for the neutralisation of sodium hydroxide by hydrochloric acid is
questions.explanation: Only the hydrogen and hydroxide ions take part in the reaction; Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are spectator ions.

questions.text: The pH of a 0.01 mol/dm³ solution of hydrochloric acid is
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid, so [H⁺] = 0.01 = 10⁻² mol/dm³ and pH = −log[H⁺] = 2.

questions.text: The oxidation number of sulphur in tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, H₂SO₄, is
Which of the following is a weak acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid only partially ionises in water. HCl, H₂SO₄ and HNO₃ are strong acids that ionise almost completely.

questions.text: 25 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide neutralises 20 cm³ of hydrochloric acid. The concentration of the acid is
questions.explanation: For the 1:1 reaction, C₁V₁ = C₂V₂, so C = 25 × 0.1 ÷ 20 = 0.125 mol/dm³.

questions.text: An aqueous solution of ammonium chloride is acidic because the salt undergoes
questions.explanation: NH₄⁺ hydrolyses in water to give H₃O⁺ ions, making the solution acidic. Salts of strong acids and weak bases give acidic solutions.

questions.text: Methyl orange indicator is yellow in an alkaline solution and
questions.explanation: Methyl orange turns red in acids and yellow in alkalis. Phenolphthalein, by contrast, is pink in alkalis and colourless in acids.

questions.text: A mixture of sand and common salt is best separated by
options: dissolving in water, filtering and evaporating
questions.explanation: Salt dissolves in water while sand does not; filtration removes the sand and evaporation recovers the salt.

questions.text: The solubility of a salt is 36 g per 100 g of water at 25 °C. The mass of the salt that will dissolve in 250 g of water at the same temperature is
For the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), an increase in pressure will
options: shift the equilibrium to the left
shift the equilibrium to the right
have no effect on the equilibrium
questions.explanation: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules — 2 moles of NH₃ against 4 moles of reactants — so the equilibrium shifts right.

questions.text: In the reaction Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, the oxidising agent is
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ gains electrons (is reduced) and causes zinc to be oxidised, so Cu²⁺ is the oxidising agent.

questions.text: At the cathode during the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) using copper electrodes, the product is
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ ions are discharged at the cathode as copper metal, while the copper anode dissolves, keeping the solution concentration constant.

questions.text: Hydrogen gas is tested in the laboratory by its
questions.explanation: A lighted splint held to hydrogen gives a characteristic pop. Oxygen relights a glowing splint and CO₂ turns limewater milky.

questions.text: A fixed mass of gas occupies 200 cm³ at 300 K. If it is heated to 600 K at constant pressure, its new volume is
questions.explanation: By Charles's law, V/T is constant, so V₂ = 200 × 600 ÷ 300 = 400 cm³.

questions.text: The quantity of electricity required to deposit one mole of copper from copper(II) ions is
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, so 2 moles of electrons (2 faradays = 2 × 96,500 C) are needed per mole of copper.

questions.text: A reaction in which heat is given out to the surroundings is described as exothermic and has a ΔH value that is
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions release heat, so the enthalpy change is negative. Endothermic reactions absorb heat and have positive ΔH.

questions.text: Tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is manufactured industrially by the
questions.explanation: The Contact process oxidises SO₂ to SO₃ over a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst and absorbs it to make H₂SO₄. The Ostwald process makes nitric acid.

questions.text: The gas that relights a glowing splint is
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion and relights a glowing splint. Hydrogen burns with a pop, and CO₂ extinguishes a burning splint.

questions.text: Sodium metal is stored under oil or kerosene because it
options: is a good conductor of heat
reacts violently with air and water
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts rapidly with oxygen and moisture in the air, so it is kept under an inert liquid to exclude both.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds contains both ionic and covalent bonds?
questions.explanation: In NH₄Cl the bond between NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻ is ionic, while the N–H bonds within the ammonium ion are covalent.

questions.text: Temporary hardness of water is caused by the presence of
questions.explanation: Dissolved Ca(HCO₃)₂ causes temporary hardness, removed by boiling. Calcium sulphate and magnesium chloride cause permanent hardness.

questions.text: Which allotrope of carbon conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite has delocalised electrons between its layers that carry current. Diamond's electrons are all fixed in covalent bonds, so it is an insulator.

questions.text: Iron is extracted from its oxide ores in the
questions.explanation: The blast furnace reduces iron oxides with carbon monoxide at high temperature. Electrolysis is used for aluminium, and the Bessemer converter makes steel.

questions.text: Rusting of iron requires the presence of both
questions.explanation: Iron rusts only when both oxygen and water are present; either alone does not cause rusting.

questions.text: Saponification, the reaction of fats and oils with concentrated alkali, produces
questions.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis of fats (triglycerides) gives salts of fatty acids — soap — and propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol).

questions.text: The approximate percentage by volume of oxygen in dry air is
questions.explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% argon and 0.03% carbon(IV) oxide by volume.

questions.text: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by
options: increasing the concentration of the reactants
raising the temperature of the reactants
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction path with lower activation energy. It does not change the equilibrium position or the temperature.

questions.text: Brass is an alloy consisting of
questions.explanation: Brass is Cu + Zn. Copper and tin make bronze, iron and carbon make steel, and aluminium and copper make duralumin.

questions.text: Ethanol, when oxidised under reflux with excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI), gives
questions.explanation: Complete oxidation of a primary alkanol under reflux yields the alkanoic acid. Distilling off the product during oxidation stops at ethanal.

questions.text: Esterification is the reaction between
options: an alkanoic acid and an alkanol
questions.explanation: An alkanoic acid reacts with an alkanol, with concentrated H₂SO₄ as catalyst, to form an ester and water.

questions.text: The cracking of long-chain petroleum fractions produces mainly
questions.explanation: Cracking breaks large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful ones such as petrol-range alkanes and alkenes for petrochemicals.

questions.text: The general formula of the alkenes is
questions.explanation: Alkenes contain one C=C double bond, giving CₙH₂ₙ. Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, and alkanols CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH.

questions.text: Ammonia is manufactured industrially by the
questions.explanation: The Haber process combines nitrogen and hydrogen at high pressure over an iron catalyst. The Contact process makes H₂SO₄ and the Solvay process makes Na₂CO₃.

questions.text: During the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride, the gas liberated at the anode is
questions.explanation: In concentrated brine, chloride ions are discharged at the anode in preference to hydroxide ions, giving chlorine gas. Hydrogen is liberated at the cathode.

questions.text: A solution that contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a given temperature is described as
questions.explanation: A saturated solution holds all the solute it can at that temperature. An unsaturated solution can dissolve more, and a supersaturated one holds more than the normal maximum.

questions.text: The percentage by mass of oxygen in calcium trioxocarbonate(IV), CaCO₃, is [Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100; oxygen contributes 48, so the percentage is 48%.

questions.text: Paper chromatography separates the components of a mixture because the components
options: move at different rates over the paper
questions.explanation: Separation depends on different solubilities in the solvent and different attractions to the paper, so components travel different distances.

questions.text: Which of the following metals is the most reactive?
questions.explanation: In the reactivity series, potassium is above calcium, magnesium and zinc; it reacts violently with water.

questions.text: Ethene decolourises bromine water because ethene
options: is unsaturated and undergoes an addition reaction
questions.explanation: The C=C double bond in ethene adds bromine across it, removing the bromine colour. Saturated alkanes do not react this way.

questions.text: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: Starch is a natural polymer of glucose made by plants. Polythene, PVC and nylon are synthetic polymers.

questions.text: The law of definite proportions states that a chemical compound always contains its constituent elements
options: in the same proportion by mass
questions.explanation: Pure water, for example, always contains hydrogen and oxygen in the mass ratio 1:8, whatever its source.

questions.text: Increasing the surface area of a solid reactant increases the reaction rate because it
questions.explanation: Powdered solids react faster than lumps because more reactant particles are exposed at the surface for collisions.

questions.text: A system is said to be in dynamic equilibrium when
options: the forward and reverse reactions proceed at the same rate
the concentrations of all substances are equal
all reactants have been used up
questions.explanation: In dynamic equilibrium both reactions continue but at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant although the system is not static.

questions.text: Which of the following gases is a major cause of acid rain?
questions.explanation: SO₂ dissolves in rainwater to form sulphurous and tetraoxosulphate(VI) acids. Oxides of nitrogen also contribute.

questions.text: Cement is manufactured mainly from
questions.explanation: Heating limestone (CaCO₃) with clay in a rotary kiln produces cement clinker. Sand and soda ash make glass, and bauxite yields aluminium.

questions.text: Hydrogen gas diffuses four times as fast as oxygen gas under the same conditions because hydrogen has
questions.explanation: By Graham's law, rate ∝ 1/√M. The ratio is √(32/2) = 4, so hydrogen, with the lower molar mass, diffuses faster.

questions.text: Oil spillage on farmland causes soil pollution mainly because the oil
options: coats soil particles and prevents air and water movement, killing plants and organisms
questions.explanation: Oil films block pores in the soil, cut off oxygen and water, and poison soil organisms, so crops cannot grow.

questions.text: The two main types of chemical bonding between atoms are
options: ionic and van der Waals bonding
questions.explanation: Atoms bond mainly by transfer of electrons (electrovalent/ionic) or sharing of electrons (covalent). Hydrogen, metallic and van der Waals forces are secondary or special types.

questions.text: Alpha particles emitted during radioactive decay are
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus (₂⁴He) with two protons and two neutrons. Beta particles are electrons and gamma rays are electromagnetic waves.
